source: low graphics long storyline mobile-related Mech game at the start you are ejected from a warship down onto a planet landing in a forest the forest is named ayush also you land with your team you have three other teammates AI you can give them commands follow assist retreat stay here or go over there and you point to a location you want them to go one of your teammates has long range weapons another one of your teammates has short range weapons and the last teammate you have has heavy weapons you have medium range normal weapons that you can upgrade by finding resources over the forest your mission is to figured out what happened to the last team that came down there are side quests you can do to get upgrades and credits in game currency the map is extremely large you can fast travel between locations but you have to unlock it by doing a main quest near the start you unlock a dropship that takes you from location to another location across the map and if fast forwards till you reach there making you go between locations quickly your enemies are red and black aliens that have plasma weapons that want to kill you and stop you

image_prompt.text: Distant structures across the forest - the drop wreck, alien nests, ridge lines - so the player can orient in an extremely large world
Resource caches through the forest that feed weapon upgrades
Broad open clearings in the forest that could be claimed and built on
Wide clearings and alien nests holding red and black plasma-armed hostiles, set back from the travel routes
Dropship pads at each major location acting as fast-travel endpoints
A landing site at the forest edge with warship drop wreckage where the player and three AI teammates come down
A single named forest, Ayush, covering an extremely large map with quest locations spread through it

layout_placement.text: Resource nodes placed through the forest for weapon upgrades
Dropship travel endpoints, locked until an early main quest unlocks them
Emitter points inside the alien nests where hostiles come from

notes: Close call between RPG and Shooter. RPG wins on the genre boundary rule - progression systems and an upgrade and currency loop rather than a pure combat loop - so only RPG was loaded and no Shooter options were considered.
The AI squad, its five command verbs, the weapon classes, the credits economy and the quest chain are systems with no spatial footprint.
P4: an extremely large world of distinct quest locations generates as separate regions.
Fast travel being gated on a main quest is progression state; the pads are placed, the lock is not expressible here.

open_questions.ask: Roughly how many distinct locations should the map hold, and is the forest the whole world or one region of it?
Is there a safe base or settlement anywhere, or is the whole map hostile forest?

coverage_missing.ask: How many locations, and is the forest the whole map?
Is there a home base or safe zone?
Extremely large is stated but unquantified - is this one region or several biomes?

answers.ask: Roughly how many distinct locations should the map hold, and is the forest the whole world or one region of it?
answers.answer: Make Ayush Forest the whole playable world, with about 6 distinct locations spread across it; this keeps the first build manageable while supporting the long storyline and dropship travel.

answers.ask: Is there a safe base or settlement anywhere, or is the whole map hostile forest?
answers.answer: Include one small safe landing-zone base near the start for the team and dropship; the rest of Ayush Forest is hostile alien territory.
